paper_title: Com² : A Causal-Guided Benchmark for Exploring Complex Commonsense Reasoning in Large Language Models
paper_abstract: Com² : A Causal-Guided Benchmark for Exploring Complex Commonsense Reasoning in Large Language Models

prior_works.title: ELG: an event logic graph
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Com² adopts the causal event graph formalism introduced by ELG—nodes as natural-language events and edges as causal relations—as the structured backbone to encode multi-hop commonsense chains for question synthesis.

prior_works.title: CauseNet: Towards a Causality Graph Extracted from the Web
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Com² seeds and diversifies its event pool by drawing k-shot exemplars from CauseNet’s large-scale causality graph, enabling broad, real-world root events for generating causal chains.

prior_works.title: The Book of Why: The New Science of Cause and Effect
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Com²’s core tasks explicitly operationalize Pearl’s causal theory—using the do-operator for interventions and counterfactual semantics—to modify causal graphs and instantiate user-relevant scenarios.

prior_works.title: RECO: Reliable causal chain reasoning via structural causal recurrent neural networks
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Com²’s Transition graphs directly incorporate RECO-identified transitive failure modes—scene drift and threshold effects—to construct chains where plausibility degrades with depth and stress-test long-range causal reasoning.

prior_works.title: e-CARE: A New Dataset for Exploring Explainable Causal Reasoning
prior_works.relationship_sentence: While e-CARE framed explainable causal reasoning on event graphs, it largely avoided multi-step decision, intervention, and counterfactual manipulations, a limitation Com² addresses by building multi-task, causally modified scenarios.

prior_works.title: The Birth of the Modern Detective Story (BMDS) dataset
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Com²-hard is constructed directly from BMDS detective narratives, leveraging their annotated clues and culprits to create decision, intervention, and counterfactual cases with interwoven evidence.

prior_works.title: A comparative study on reasoning patterns of OpenAI’s o1 model
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Com² attaches guided ‘slow thinking’ rationales structured around systematic analysis, divide-and-conquer, self-refinement, and context identification as outlined by Wu et al., aligning explanations to the modified causal graphs.

synthesis_narrative: Event-graph representations made causal commonsense chains concrete: ELG defined a graph formalism where natural-language events are nodes connected by causal edges, enabling structured multi-hop reasoning over implicit knowledge. CauseNet supplied a web-extracted causality graph at scale, making it practical to sample diverse, realistic root events and edges for broad coverage. Pearl’s causal theory contributed the precise operations—interventions via the do-operator and counterfactual semantics—that let one alter causal structures to pose what-if and shock-scenario questions with clear groundings. RECO pinpointed where transitive causal reasoning breaks down, introducing scene drift and threshold effects as concrete failure modes that emerge as chains lengthen and contexts shift. The BMDS detective corpus provided richly interwoven clues and annotated culprits, furnishing a narrative substrate for complex, evidence-based decision and counterfactual cases. Finally, analyses of slow-thinking patterns in o1 by Wu et al. articulated actionable reasoning scaffolds—systematic analysis, divide-and-conquer, self-refinement, and context identification—that can be embedded as guided rationales. Together, these works revealed both how to structure causal knowledge and where models falter as dependencies deepen or shift. Com² naturally synthesizes these insights by (i) using event graphs as the backbone, (ii) applying Pearl’s do- and counterfactual operators to generate user-relevant scenarios, (iii) instantiating RECO’s failure modes to probe transitive robustness, (iv) leveraging CauseNet and BMDS to source realistic and narratively complex contexts, and (v) attaching Wu-style slow-thinking traces guided by the graphs. This directly addresses e-CARE’s gap by delivering a multi-task benchmark that stresses depth, breadth, and hypothetical reasoning in complex commonsense.

innovation_classification.reasoning: Constructs a causal commonsense benchmark using event-graph representations and Pearl-style interventions/counterfactuals.
